exposure: Species (Sprague-Dawley rat, New Zealand White rabbit, Gottingen minipig)
outcome: Frequency of external malformations and variations
Frequency of visceral malformations and variations
Frequency of skeletal malformations and variations
cohort: The study included pregnant female Sprague-Dawley rats (n=824), New Zealand White rabbits (n=540), and Gottingen minipigs (n=70) from vehicle control groups, equating to 10,749 rat, 5,073 rabbit, and 378 pig fetuses.
finding: Significant species-dependent differences exist in the relative incidence of spontaneous variations and malformations, particularly with visceral malformations of the heart and major blood vessels being remarkably more frequent in minipigs and rabbits compared to rats.
